title: Mexports reach 2026 peak in August before seasonal decline, says Wood Mackenzie
gist: US natural gas pipeline exports to Mexico closed August 2026 at a record monthly average of almost 7.9 Bcf/d, driven by all-time highs from West Texas (approaching 2.3 Bcf/d on 13 August) and South Texas (crossing 5.4 Bcf/d on 26 August) and by record Mexican gas burn for power of over 5.8 Bcf/d. Wood Mackenzie calls this the 2026 peak and expects a seasonal decline from here, while maintaining that the medium-term trajectory stays upward as Mexico's combined-cycle fleet expands.

insights.claim: US natural gas pipeline exports to Mexico closed August 2026 at a record monthly average of almost 7.9 Bcf/d.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sets the benchmark level for the largest single export outlet of US pipeline gas; deviations from ~7.9 Bcf/d reset the Waha and South Texas basis picture.
insights.quote: US natural gas pipeline exports to Mexico (Mexports) are closing August at a record monthly average of almost 7.9 Bcf/d
insights.locator: US natural gas pipeline exports to Mexico

insights.claim: West Texas and South Texas are the primary drivers behind the record, with both regions simultaneously posting all-time highs in monthly averages and single-day flows.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Concentrated regional sourcing means Permian and South Texas takeaway economics, not aggregate US supply, set the ceiling on Mexican export growth.
insights.quote: Incremental volumes from West Texas (WTX) and South Texas (STX) are the primary drivers behind this milestone.

insights.claim: On gas day 13 August West Texas flows to Mexico approached 2.3 Bcf/d, and on 26 August South Texas crossed the 5.4 Bcf/d mark.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Single-day peaks define practical corridor capacity - useful ceilings when modelling how much more export growth existing pipe can absorb.
insights.quote: On gas day 13 August, WTX approached 2.3 Bcf/d; on 26 August, STX crossed the 5.4 Bcf/d mark.

themes.theme: Power burn as the demand engine

insights.claim: Natural gas burn for power generation is the main demand factor behind Mexport growth and set a new all-time monthly average of over 5.8 Bcf/d in August 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Roughly three-quarters of record Mexport volume traces to power burn, so Mexican electricity demand - not industrial or residential gas - is the variable to track.
insights.quote: Natural gas burns for power generation, the main demand factor for Mexports' growth, set a new all-time monthly average of over 5.8 Bcf/d in August.
insights.locator: Natural gas burns for power generation

insights.claim: The August record reflects two distinct forces that should be separated when forecasting - the structural growth of Mexico's gas-fired power sector and the cyclical intensity of this year's cooling season.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Only the structural half persists; extrapolating the full August print into 2027 overstates baseline demand growth.
insights.quote: August's record Mexport flows reflect both the structural growth of Mexico's gas-fired power sector and the intensity of this year's cooling season.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie projects that Mexican gas import volumes have now reached their 2026 peak, with a downward push likely to develop soon even though volumes remained strong in early September.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: An explicit call that the annual high is in - a directional short signal for South Texas and Waha basis strength tied to export pull.
insights.quote: Wood Mackenzie projects Mexports have now reached their 2026 peak.
insights.locator: Wood Mackenzie projects Mexports have now reached

insights.claim: Three specific mechanisms will drive the coming decline in Mexican gas and power demand: easing cooling loads, shoulder-season maintenance windows, and holiday-related demand softness.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A named checklist for timing the fade - maintenance schedules and holiday calendars are observable ahead of the flow data.
insights.quote: driven by easing cooling loads, shoulder-season maintenance windows, and holiday-related demand softness
insights.locator: From here, Mexican gas and power markets

insights.claim: Despite the near-term seasonal decline, the medium-term trajectory for US gas exports to Mexico remains upward as Mexico's combined-cycle fleet continues to expand.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Separates a tactical short from a structural long - combined-cycle build-out is the multi-year anchor for US Gulf and Permian gas demand.
insights.quote: The medium-term trajectory, however, remains upward as Mexico's combined-cycle fleet continues to expand
